import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’ll trace the prompt-search path, measure where it spends time, and use the `/sase_plan` skill to author, validate, and submit a plan before changing implementation files.


Search currently loads the full prompt corpus before matching or applying the result limit. I’m checking how much of the delay comes from loading history versus matching, and how the Rust core should support the fix. I’m also using `/sase_memory_read` and `/sase_repo` for the required project guidance and repository access.


I found a concrete problem: archive inventory runs the full archive validator, including checking links and hashing artifact files, and search then rereads every prompt. Those checks are unnecessary for searching. I’m measuring that cost alongside local-history loading so the plan targets the largest delays.


There’s a second avoidable cost in `--format full`: each displayed local hit reloads the entire history to resolve its ID. I’ll include that in the plan. The measurements are still running; the workspace’s Rust extension was unavailable, so I’m profiling the checkout with the working installed runtime without changing dependencies.


The profile exposed a more severe issue: for prompts containing Unicode and many code fences, Python rebuilds a character-offset map for the entire prompt separately for every fence range. A search was still doing this after more than a minute. I’m testing an in-memory optimization to confirm the speedup; no source files have changed.


The corpus has about 5,000 archived prompts and 7,800 local records. With temporary in-memory reuse of offset maps and metadata parsing, collection finishes in about 5.8 seconds; matching takes only 0.08 seconds. That points to preprocessing as the main target. I’m checking whether converting only the needed offsets can cut collection further before choosing the final scope.


Converting only the needed offsets and parsing metadata once brings collection to about 3.3 seconds in the experiment. The unchanged version exceeded the 12-second cutoff, so this is a promising result, not a completed benchmark.

I’m choosing a `tale` plan with `size: medium`: a bounded set of fixes to offset conversion, metadata reuse, archive loading, and full-output rendering. The plan will preserve search behavior and require measured speedups and regression tests before completion.


The medium tale plan passed validation, was refined, and passed revalidation with zero warnings. It requires at least a 5× speedup on a representative corpus, exact search-result compatibility, and coverage for Unicode offsets, archive validation, and full-output history loading.

I’m checking that the repositories remain unchanged, then submitting it with `sase plan propose`.
